generated_for: a learner studying this material at the level, goal and pace in their learner profile.

fact-ledger.check: level-independent reference. Use it to check a fact or find its source location; the lesson is the explained reading.

lesson.check: adapted to the learner profile. Pictures and tables first, definitions in the words the profile asks for, an example per idea. Left out: only what the goal does not test; the fact ledger keeps every fact.

quiz.check: difficulty set by the learner profile; hints on request; nothing outside the source material is tested.

answer-key.check: every wrong option is explained, with the source location of the fact; open it after answering.

concept-map.check: same facts as the chapters; wording kept plain; no facts dropped.

cram-sheet.check: same facts as the chapters; wording kept plain; no facts dropped.

final-quiz.check: cumulative across all chapters; hints on request; misses go to the revisit list.

final-quiz-key.check: cumulative across all chapters; open it after answering.

score-tracker.check: same facts as the chapters; wording kept plain; no facts dropped.

revisit-list.check: same facts as the chapters; wording kept plain; no facts dropped.

README.check: a plain-language guide to the files; no facts changed.

review.check: each explanation names the exact trap, not only the answer.

mock-exam.check: exam-style practice; scored in one sitting; misses go to the revisit list.

mock-exam-key.check: open only after you finish the exam.

domain-exam.check: exam-style practice; take it in one sitting, then use the key to find weak chapters and add them to the revisit list.

domain-exam-key.check: open only after you finish the exam; each miss points back to the chapter to revisit.
